sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vistareṇārthasaṃbandhaṃ śrotum icchāmi pārthiva mitradrohī kṛtaghnaś ca yaḥ proktas taṃ ca me vada
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I wish to hear in full, O king, the matter and its connection. Tell me too of that man whom you have called a betrayer of friends and ungrateful.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca hanta te vartayiṣye 'ham itihāsaṃ purātanam udīcyāṃ diśi yad vṛttaṃ mleccheṣu manujādhipa
english: Bhīṣma said: Come, I shall recount to you an ancient tale of what once came to pass in the northern region, among the barbarian peoples, O lord of men.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo madhyadeśīyaḥ kṛṣṇāṅgo brahmavarjitaḥ grāmaṃ prekṣya janākīrṇaṃ prāviśad bhaikṣakāṅkṣayā
english: A brāhmaṇa from the Middle Country, dark of limb and devoid of sacred learning, spying a village thronged with people, entered it in hope of alms.

sanskrit: tatra dasyur dhanayutaḥ sarvavarṇaviśeṣavit brahmaṇyaḥ satyasaṃdhaś ca dāne ca nirato 'bhavat
english: There dwelt a robber, rich in wealth, knowing well the distinctions of all the classes, devoted to brāhmaṇas, true to his word, and given to charity.

sanskrit: tasya kṣayam upāgamya tato bhikṣām ayācata pratiśrayaṃ ca vāsārthaṃ bhikṣāṃ caivātha vārṣikīm
english: Coming to his dwelling, the brāhmaṇa then begged of him: a shelter to live in, and alms enough to last the year.

sanskrit: prādāt tasmai sa viprāya vastraṃ ca sadṛśaṃ navam nārīṃ cāpi vayopetāṃ bhartrā virahitāṃ tadā
english: To that brāhmaṇa he gave fresh garments, fitting and fine, and also a woman in the bloom of her years, who was then bereft of her husband.

sanskrit: etat saṃprāpya hṛṣṭātmā dasyoḥ sarvaṃ dvijas tadā tasmin gṛhavare rājaṃs tayā reme sa gautamaḥ
english: Having received all this from the robber, the twice-born one, glad at heart, then dwelt in that fine house, O king, and took his pleasure with her — this Gautama.

sanskrit: kuṭumbārtheṣu dasyoḥ sa sāhāyyaṃ cāpy athākarot tatrāvasat so 'tha varṣāḥ samṛddhe śabarālaye bāṇavedhye paraṃ yatnam akaroc caiva gautamaḥ
english: He even lent his aid to the robber in the affairs of his household, and so he dwelt there through the rains in that prosperous abode of the Śabaras; and Gautama applied himself with the utmost effort to piercing the mark with arrows.

sanskrit: vakrāṅgāṃs tu sa nityaṃ vai sarvato bāṇagocare jaghāna gautamo rājan yathā dasyugaṇas tathā
english: And the crooked-limbed birds that came within range of his arrows, on every side, this Gautama slew without ceasing, O king, just as the robber band would do.

sanskrit: hiṃsāparo ghṛṇāhīnaḥ sadā prāṇivadhe rataḥ gautamaḥ saṃnikarṣeṇa dasyubhiḥ samatām iyāt
english: Bent on violence, void of pity, ever delighting in the slaughter of living things, Gautama, through his close company with the robbers, grew to be the equal of them.

sanskrit: tathā tu vasatas tasya dasyugrāme sukhaṃ tadā agacchan bahavo māsā nighnataḥ pakṣiṇo bahūn
english: As he dwelt thus at ease in the robbers' village, many months went by while he killed great numbers of birds.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid aparo dvijas taṃ deśam āgamat jaṭī cīrājinadharaḥ svādhyāyaparamaḥ śuciḥ
english: Then on a certain day another twice-born one came to that country: matted of hair, clad in bark-cloth and deerskin, supreme in the study of the Veda, and pure.

sanskrit: vinīto niyatāhāro brahmaṇyo vedapāragaḥ sabrahmacārī taddeśyaḥ sakhā tasyaiva supriyam taṃ dasyugrāmam agamad yatrāsau gautamo 'bhavat
english: Humble, restrained in his eating, devoted to the brāhmaṇas, master of the Veda to its far shore — a fellow student of Gautama, born of that same land, and his very dear friend — he came to that robbers' village where Gautama had settled.

sanskrit: sa tu vipragṛhānveṣī śūdrānnaparivarjakaḥ grāme dasyujanākīrṇe vyacarat sarvatodiśam
english: Seeking out the house of a brāhmaṇa, shunning the food of Śūdras, he wandered in every direction through that village crowded with robber folk.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa gautamagṛhaṃ praviveśa dvijottamaḥ gautamaś cāpi saṃprāptas tāv anyonyena saṃgatau
english: Then that best of the twice-born entered Gautama's house, and Gautama too returned, and the two were brought together once more.

sanskrit: vakrāṅgabhārahastaṃ taṃ dhanuṣpāṇiṃ kṛtāgasam rudhireṇāvasiktāṅgaṃ gṛhadvāram upāgatam
english: He saw Gautama come to the door of the house, his hands laden with crooked-limbed birds, his bow in his grip, a doer of sinful deeds, his limbs spattered with blood —

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā puruṣādābham apadhvastaṃ kṣayāgatam abhijñāya dvijo vrīḍām agamad vākyam āha ca
english: and seeing him, like a man-eating fiend, fallen and ruined as he came to his dwelling, the twice-born one knew him, and was overcome with shame, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: kim idaṃ kuruṣe mauḍhyād vipras tvaṃ hi kulodgataḥ madhyadeśaparijñāto dasyubhāvaṃ gataḥ katham
english: "What is this you do in your folly? You are a brāhmaṇa, sprung of a noble line, well known in the Middle Country. How have you sunk to the ways of a robber?

sanskrit: pūrvān smara dvijāgryāṃs tān prakhyātān vedapāragān yeṣāṃ vaṃśe 'bhijātas tvam īdṛśaḥ kulapāṃsanaḥ
english: Remember those foremost of brāhmaṇas, your forebears, renowned, masters of the Veda, in whose line you were born — you, such a disgrace to your family!

sanskrit: avabudhyātmanātmānaṃ satyaṃ śīlaṃ śrutaṃ damam anukrośaṃ ca saṃsmṛtya tyaja vāsam imaṃ dvija
english: Come to know your own self by yourself, and calling to mind truth, good conduct, sacred learning, self-restraint, and compassion, abandon this dwelling, O twice-born one."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa suhṛdā tadā tena hitaiṣiṇā pratyuvāca tato rājan viniścitya tadārtavat
english: Thus addressed by his friend, who sought his good, he then answered, O king, having made up his mind, and as one in distress:

sanskrit: adhano 'smi dvijaśreṣṭha na ca vedavid apy aham vṛttyartham iha saṃprāptaṃ viddhi māṃ dvijasattama
english: "I am without wealth, O best of the twice-born, nor am I a knower of the Veda. Know me, O finest of brāhmaṇas, to have come here for the sake of a livelihood.

sanskrit: tvaddarśanāt tu viprarṣe kṛtārthaṃ vedmy ahaṃ dvija ātmānaṃ saha yāsyāvaḥ śvo vasādyeha śarvarīm
english: But by the sight of you, O sage among brāhmaṇas, I count my purpose fulfilled, O twice-born one. We shall go forth together; only stay here this night, and tomorrow we depart."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tasyāṃ niśāyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ gate tasmin dvijottame niṣkramya gautamo 'gacchat samudraṃ prati bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: When that night had passed away and the best of the twice-born had gone, Gautama set out and made his way toward the sea, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: sāmudrakān sa vaṇijas tato 'paśyat sthitān pathi sa tena sārthena saha prayayau sāgaraṃ prati
english: Then he saw seafaring merchants halted along the road, and with that caravan he journeyed on toward the ocean.

sanskrit: sa tu sārtho mahārāja kasmiṃś cid girigahvare mattena dviradenātha nihataḥ prāyaśo 'bhavat
english: But that caravan, O great king, in a certain mountain ravine was set upon by a rutting elephant and very nearly destroyed.

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ cit tatas tasmāt sārthān mukto dvijas tadā kāṃdigbhūto jīvitārthī pradudrāvottarāṃ diśam
english: The brāhmaṇa, freed somehow from that caravan, bewildered and clinging to his life, fled away to the north.

sanskrit: sa sarvataḥ paribhraṣṭaḥ sārthād deśāt tathārthataḥ ekākī vyadravat tatra vane kiṃpuruṣo yathā
english: Cut off on every side — from caravan, from the country, and from his goods — he ran on there alone through the forest, like a wild Kiṃpuruṣa.

sanskrit: sa panthānam athāsādya samudrābhisaraṃ tadā āsasāda vanaṃ ramyaṃ mahat puṣpitapādapam
english: Then, lighting upon a path that ran down toward the sea, he came at last to a lovely, vast forest with trees in flower.

sanskrit: sarvartukair āmravanaiḥ puṣpitair upaśobhitam nandanoddeśasadṛśaṃ yakṣakiṃnarasevitam
english: It was made beautiful by groves of mango trees blossoming in every season — like a tract of Nandana itself, haunted by Yakṣas and Kiṃnaras.

sanskrit: śālatāladhavāśvatthatvacāguruvanais tathā candanasya ca mukhyasya pādapair upaśobhitam giriprastheṣu ramyeṣu śubheṣu susugandhiṣu
english: It was graced with woods of śāla and tāla, of dhava and aśvattha, of cinnamon-bark and aloe, and with trees of the finest sandalwood, upon lovely, fair, and sweetly fragrant mountain slopes.

sanskrit: samantato dvijaśreṣṭhā valgu kūjanti tatra vai manuṣyavadanās tv anye bhāruṇḍā iti viśrutāḥ bhūliṅgaśakunāś cānye samudraṃ sarvato 'bhavan
english: On every side the noblest of birds sang there sweetly; and others, with the faces of men, were known as Bhāruṇḍas; and still others, the Bhūliṅga birds, were all about the sea.

sanskrit: sa tāny atimanojñāni vihaṃgābhirutāni vai śṛṇvan suramaṇīyāni vipro 'gacchata gautamaḥ
english: Listening to those most charming and delightful songs of the birds, the brāhmaṇa Gautama went onward.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyat suramye sa suvarṇasikatācite deśabhāge same citre svargoddeśasamaprabhe
english: Then he beheld, in a most lovely spot — a level, varied stretch of land strewn with golden sand, bright as a region of heaven —

sanskrit: śriyā juṣṭaṃ mahāvṛkṣaṃ nyagrodhaṃ parimaṇḍalam śākhābhir anurūpābhir bhūṣitaṃ chatrasaṃnibham
english: a great tree endowed with splendor, a banyan, perfectly rounded, adorned with shapely branches, and shaped like a parasol.

sanskrit: tasya mūlaṃ susaṃsiktaṃ varacandanavāriṇā divyapuṣpānvitaṃ śrīmat pitāmahasadopamam
english: Its root was well sprinkled with water scented by the finest sandal, decked with divine flowers, glorious — like the very court of the Grandsire.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā gautamaḥ prīto munikāntam anuttamam medhyaṃ suragṛhaprakhyaṃ puṣpitaiḥ pādapair vṛtam tam āgamya mudā yuktas tasyādhastād upāviśat
english: Seeing that tree — peerless, dear to the sages, holy, like the dwelling of a god, and ringed by flowering trees — Gautama was glad, and coming up to it with joy, he sat down beneath it.

sanskrit: tatrāsīnasya kauravya gautamasya sukhaḥ śivaḥ puṣpāṇi samupaspṛśya pravavāv anilaḥ śuciḥ hlādayan sarvagātrāṇi gautamasya tadā nṛpa
english: As Gautama sat there, O Kaurava, a pure breeze, soft and kindly, having touched the flowers, blew gently, refreshing all the limbs of Gautama, O king.

sanskrit: sa tu vipraḥ pariśrāntaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ puṇyena vāyunā sukham āsādya suṣvāpa bhāskaraś cāstam abhyagāt
english: And the brāhmaṇa, weary and touched by that hallowed wind, finding ease, fell asleep; and the sun went down to its setting.

sanskrit: tato 'staṃ bhāskare yāte saṃdhyākāla upasthite ājagāma svabhavanaṃ brahmalokāt khagottamaḥ
english: Then, when the sun had set and the hour of twilight had come, the best of birds came home to his own abode from the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: nāḍījaṅgha iti khyāto dayito brahmaṇaḥ sakhā bakarājo mahāprājñaḥ kaśyapasyātmasaṃbhavaḥ
english: He was renowned as Nāḍījaṅgha, the beloved friend of Brahmā, a king among cranes, vast in wisdom, sprung from the very being of Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: rājadharmeti vikhyāto babhūvāpratimo bhuvi devakanyāsutaḥ śrīmān vidvān devapatiprabhaḥ
english: Famed as Rājadharma, he was without equal upon the earth — the son of a daughter of the gods, glorious, learned, and radiant as the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: mṛṣṭahāṭakasaṃchanno bhūṣaṇair arkasaṃnibhaiḥ bhūṣitaḥ sarvagātreṣu devagarbhaḥ śriyā jvalan
english: Covered with burnished gold, adorned upon all his limbs with ornaments bright as the sun, born of divine seed, he blazed with splendor.

sanskrit: tam āgataṃ dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismito gautamo 'bhavat kṣutpipāsāparītātmā hiṃsārthī cāpy avaikṣata
english: Seeing that bird arrive, Gautama was filled with wonder; yet, his spirit overcome by hunger and thirst, he looked upon him with intent to kill.

sanskrit: rājadharmovāca svāgataṃ bhavate vipra diṣṭyā prāpto 'si me gṛham astaṃ ca savitā yātaḥ saṃdhyeyaṃ samupasthitā
english: Rājadharma said: Welcome to you, O brāhmaṇa! By good fortune you have come to my home. The sun has gone to its setting, and this twilight is now upon us.

sanskrit: mama tvaṃ nilayaṃ prāptaḥ priyātithir aninditaḥ pūjito yāsyasi prātar vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: You have come to my dwelling, a welcome and blameless guest; honored with rites as the ordinance prescribes, you shall go your way in the morning.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca giraṃ tāṃ madhurāṃ śrutvā gautamo vismitas tadā kautūhalānvito rājan rājadharmāṇam aikṣata
english: Bhīṣma said: Hearing that sweet speech, Gautama then was amazed, and filled with curiosity, O king, he gazed upon Rājadharma.

sanskrit: rājadharmovāca bhoḥ kaśyapasya putro 'haṃ mātā dākṣāyaṇī ca me atithis tvaṃ guṇopetaḥ svāgataṃ te dvijarṣabha
english: Rājadharma said: Sir, I am the son of Kaśyapa, and my mother is a daughter of Dakṣa. You are my guest, endowed with virtues — welcome to you, O bull among the twice-born!

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tasmai dattvā sa satkāraṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā śālapuṣpamayīṃ divyāṃ bṛsīṃ samupakalpayat
english: Bhīṣma said: Having paid him honor with rites as the ordinance prescribes, he made ready for him a divine seat fashioned of śāla blossoms.

sanskrit: bhagīratharathākrāntān deśān gaṅgāniṣevitān ye caranti mahāmīnās tāṃś ca tasyānvakalpayat
english: And he procured for him great fishes — such as range the regions watered by the Gaṅgā, the tracts once traversed by Bhagīratha's chariot.

sanskrit: vahniṃ cāpi susaṃdīptaṃ mīnāṃś caiva supīvarān sa gautamāyātithaye nyavedayata kāśyapaḥ
english: A well-kindled fire, too, and fishes good and plump did the son of Kaśyapa set before Gautama, his guest.

sanskrit: bhuktavantaṃ ca taṃ vipraṃ prītātmānaṃ mahāmanāḥ klamāpanayanārthaṃ sa pakṣābhyām abhyavījayat
english: And when the brāhmaṇa had eaten and was content at heart, the great-souled bird, to take away his weariness, fanned him with his two wings.

sanskrit: tato viśrāntam āsīnaṃ gotrapraśnam apṛcchata so 'bravīd gautamo 'smīti brāhma nānyad udāharat
english: Then, as the brāhmaṇa sat rested, the bird asked him the question of his lineage; and he said only, "I am of the Gautama gotra," and gave no other account of himself.

sanskrit: tasmai parṇamayaṃ divyaṃ divyapuṣpādhivāsitam gandhāḍhyaṃ śayanaṃ prādāt sa śiśye tatra vai sukham
english: For him he made ready a divine couch of leaves, perfumed with heavenly flowers and rich with fragrance; and there indeed he lay at ease.

sanskrit: athopaviṣṭaṃ śayane gautamaṃ bakarāṭ tadā papraccha kāśyapo vāgmī kim āgamanakāraṇam
english: Then, as Gautama sat upon the couch, the king of cranes, the eloquent son of Kaśyapa, asked him the reason for his coming.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd gautamas taṃ daridro 'haṃ mahāmate samudragamanākāṅkṣī dravyārtham iti bhārata
english: Then Gautama answered him: "I am a poor man, O great-minded one. I long to go to the sea for the sake of wealth, O descendant of Bharata."

sanskrit: taṃ kāśyapo 'bravīt prīto notkaṇṭhāṃ kartum arhasi kṛtakāryo dvijaśreṣṭha sadravyo yāsyase gṛhān
english: The son of Kaśyapa, well pleased, said to him: "You ought not to be troubled. Your end accomplished, O best of the twice-born, and laden with wealth, you shall return to your home.

sanskrit: caturvidhā hy arthagatir bṛhaspatimataṃ yathā pāraṃparyaṃ tathā daivaṃ karma mitram iti prabho
english: For the winning of wealth is fourfold, according to the teaching of Bṛhaspati: by inheritance, by fate, by one's own effort, and by a friend, O lord.

sanskrit: prādurbhūto 'smi te mitraṃ suhṛttvaṃ ca mama tvayi so 'haṃ tathā yatiṣyāmi bhaviṣyasi yathārthavān
english: I have shown myself to be your friend, and my heart is friendly toward you. I shall so strive that you will come to be a man of wealth."

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhātasamaye sukhaṃ pṛṣṭvābravīd idam gaccha saumya pathānena kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi
english: Then, at the hour of dawn, having asked after his rest, the bird spoke thus: "Go, gentle sir, by this path, and you shall attain your purpose.

sanskrit: itas triyojanaṃ gatvā rākṣasādhipatir mahān virūpākṣa iti khyātaḥ sakhā mama mahābalaḥ
english: Go three yojanas from here, and you will find a great lord of the Rākṣasas, renowned as Virūpākṣa, my friend, of mighty strength.

sanskrit: taṃ gaccha dvijamukhya tvaṃ mama vākyapracoditaḥ kāmān abhīpsitāṃs tubhyaṃ dātā nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: Go to him, O chief of the twice-born, prompted by my word; he will grant you the desires of your heart — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ prayayau rājan gautamo vigataklamaḥ phalāny amṛtakalpāni bhakṣayan sma yatheṣṭataḥ
english: Thus addressed, Gautama set forth, O king, his weariness gone, eating at his pleasure fruits that were like the nectar of immortality.

sanskrit: candanāgurumukhyāni tvakpatrāṇāṃ vanāni ca tasmin pathi mahārāja sevamāno drutaṃ yayau
english: Passing along that road, O great king, amid groves of sandal and aloe and the choicest cinnamon-bark and leaf, he went swiftly on.

sanskrit: tato meruvrajaṃ nāma nagaraṃ śailatoraṇam śailaprākāravapraṃ ca śailayantrārgalaṃ tathā
english: Then he came to a city named Meruvraja, with gateways of rock, with ramparts and bulwarks of rock, and barred with engines and bolts of rock.

sanskrit: viditaś cābhavat tasya rākṣasendrasya dhīmataḥ prahitaḥ suhṛdā rājan prīyatā vai priyātithiḥ
english: And he became known to that wise lord of the Rākṣasas — sent by a friend, O king, a welcome guest to be cherished.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rākṣasendraḥ svān preṣyān āha yudhiṣṭhira gautamo nagaradvārāc chīghram ānīyatām iti
english: Then that lord of the Rākṣasas said to his own servants, O Yudhiṣṭhira: "Let Gautama be brought in swiftly from the city gate."

sanskrit: tataḥ puravarāt tasmāt puruṣāḥ śvetaveṣṭanāḥ gautamety abhibhāṣantaḥ puradvāram upāgaman
english: Then from that fair city men with white turbans came to the city gate, calling out, "Gautama! Gautama!"

sanskrit: te tam ūcur mahārāja preṣyā rakṣaḥpater dvijam tvarasva tūrṇam āgaccha rājā tvāṃ draṣṭum icchati
english: Those servants of the Rākṣasa lord said to the brāhmaṇa, O great king: "Make haste, come quickly, the king wishes to see you.

sanskrit: rākṣasādhipatir vīro virūpākṣa iti śrutaḥ sa tvāṃ tvarati vai draṣṭuṃ tat kṣipraṃ saṃvidhīyatām
english: The lord of the Rākṣasas, the hero known as Virūpākṣa, is eager to see you; therefore let it be done at once."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa prādravad vipro vismayād vigataklamaḥ gautamo nagararddhiṃ tāṃ paśyan paramavismitaḥ
english: Then the brāhmaṇa hurried forward, his weariness gone in his wonder, gazing in utter amazement upon the splendor of that city.

sanskrit: tair eva sahito rājño veśma tūrṇam upādravat darśanaṃ rākṣasendrasya kāṅkṣamāṇo dvijas tadā
english: In their company he hastened swiftly to the king's palace, that brāhmaṇa then longing for the sight of the lord of the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ sa vidito rājñaḥ praviśya gṛham uttamam pūjito rākṣasendreṇa niṣasādāsanottame
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, announced to the king, he entered that noble palace and, honored by the lord of the Rākṣasas, sat down upon an excellent seat.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭaś ca gotracaraṇaṃ svādhyāyaṃ brahmacārikam na tatra vyājahārānyad gotramātrād ṛte dvijaḥ
english: And being asked of his lineage and observance, his Vedic study and his life of chastity, the brāhmaṇa there said nothing beyond his gotra alone.

sanskrit: brahmavarcasahīnasya svādhyāyaviratasya ca gotramātravido rājā nivāsaṃ samapṛcchata
english: Of him who was bereft of the lustre of sacred learning and had ceased from Vedic study, who knew only his gotra, the king then inquired about his dwelling-place.

sanskrit: kva te nivāsaḥ kalyāṇa kiṃgotrā brāhmaṇī ca te tattvaṃ brūhi na bhīḥ kāryā viśramasva yathāsukham
english: "Where is your dwelling, good sir? And of what gotra is your brāhmaṇa wife? Tell me the truth, you need have no fear; rest at your ease."

sanskrit: gautama uvāca madhyadeśaprasūto 'haṃ vāso me śabarālaye śūdrā punarbhūr bhāryā me satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Gautama said: "I was born in the Middle Country; my dwelling is in an abode of the Śabaras. My wife is a Śūdra woman, once wedded before — this truth I tell you."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato rājā vimamṛśe kathaṃ kāryam idaṃ bhavet kathaṃ vā sukṛtaṃ me syād iti buddhyānvacintayat
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the king pondered: "How is this matter to be handled? And how may a good deed be wrought by me?" — so he considered in his mind.

sanskrit: ayaṃ vai jananād vipraḥ suhṛt tasya mahātmanaḥ saṃpreṣitaś ca tenāyaṃ kāśyapena mamāntikam
english: "This man is a brāhmaṇa by birth, the friend of that great-souled one, and he has been sent to my presence by that son of Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: tasya priyaṃ kariṣyāmi sa hi mām āśritaḥ sadā bhrātā me bāndhavaś cāsau sakhā ca hṛdayaṃgamaḥ
english: I shall do what is dear to him, for he has ever leaned upon me; he is my brother, my kinsman, and a friend who has won my heart."
